readmeHtml:
Apache Maka (Incubating)

简体中文

Apache Maka (Incubating) is a local-first agent workspace for the terminal and desktop. A background Rust Runtime Host owns model execution, sandboxing, permissions, and SQLite state, keeping an auditable record of every run, approval, and tool receipt.

Quick start

Prerequisites: Rust stable, Node.js 24+ (CI uses 26), npm, and just. Native Computer Use also requires Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS or X11 development libraries on Linux.

git clone https://github.com/apache/maka.git
cd maka
just setup
just run

just run launches the terminal workbench and connects to (or starts) the local Host at ~/.maka/application/host. Pass --root <path> to use a different State Root, --session <id> to open an existing conversation, or --help to inspect CLI subcommands.

To build release binaries for both the CLI and the native desktop window:

just build --release
target/release/maka desktop

On macOS, just build stages Maka.app alongside maka; on Windows, binaries carry .exe. Both the terminal and desktop shells run the same NSH workbench UI against the same Host process—closing the window detaches the UI while in-flight work finishes in the background.

In WSL, just run skips the Linux native-desktop feature and bridges Computer Use to the Windows desktop by default. Point MAKA_CUA_WINDOWS_EXECUTABLE to a matching Windows maka.exe when running from source; see Computer Use.

Repository layout

Directory Role
platform/ Plugin kernel, SQLite event log, Host runtime, V8/Python sandboxes, OS isolation, and Computer Use
plugins/ Agent runtime, workspace tools, skills, settings, interactions, and shared domain contracts
products/maka/ Product composition, NSH workbench, CLI, ACP server, and terminal/desktop shells
products/eval/ Containerized Harbor evaluation runner against the native Host
packages/plugin-sdk/ Generated TypeScript contracts and helpers for Host and NSH UI plugins
packages/cli/ @maka-agent/cli npm launcher for platform-native binaries
scripts/rust/ Native packaging, V8 prebuilt management, license checks, and CI suite runner
website/ Project website (independent package manifest and lockfile)

Run just --list to see common development recipes. Further reading: Architecture, UI Design, Contributing, and Security.

Distribution

Apache Releases: The latest approved release is Apache Maka 0.2.2 (incubating). The signed source archive is the official release; see the downloads page and .github/ASF_SOURCE_RELEASE.md for verification instructions.

Convenience builds: @maka-agent/cli is a thin npm wrapper that dispatches to a platform-specific native binary package built from a single verified source archive; see packages/cli.

Apache Maka is an effort undergoing incubation at The Apache Software Foundation (ASF). See DISCLAIMER, LICENSE, and NOTICE.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A local-first AI agent workspace that records model messages and tool executions as an append-only log.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Maka is a local-first workspace designed for executing and auditing complex AI agent tasks. It replaces ephemeral chat contexts with a durable, append-only Runtime Event Log that strictly records all model messages, tool calls, permission decisions, and execution results. This architecture ensures that every agent interaction—whether inspecting projects or generating artifacts—is highly transparent, recoverable, and reproducible. By keeping sessions and settings on the local machine and allowing flexible model connections (cloud API or local), it provides a secure environment for agents to perform real work while remaining fully auditable.
keyFeatures: Append-Only Execution Log: Record every model message, tool call, and termination event as immutable facts in a durable runtime log.
Local-First Architecture: Store all sessions, configurations, and run records locally to maintain data privacy and offline capability.
Flexible Model Support: Connect seamlessly to cloud APIs, locally hosted models, or compatible gateways without changing the core workflow.
Multi-Interface Access: Execute agent tasks via a dedicated macOS desktop app, a terminal TUI, or a non-interactive CLI.
Auditable Tool Execution: Enforce controlled permissions and explicitly log every tool invocation and result for complete execution transparency.

useCases.title: Auditable Agent Workflows
useCases.description: Running complex, multi-step agent tasks where every tool execution and state change must be verifiable and reversible.

useCases.title: Local-First Development
useCases.description: Executing AI coding assistants on private, sensitive codebases without exposing the execution context to a hosted cloud workspace.

useCases.title: Agent Evaluation Tracking
useCases.description: Using the append-only event log to precisely analyze an agent's decision-making process and tool usage for model evaluation.

useCases.title: Recoverable AI Sessions
useCases.description: Resuming long-running, interrupted agent tasks flawlessly by replaying the deterministic execution log from the local machine.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: AI engineers, security-conscious developers, and researchers who require an auditable, local-first environment to run and evaluate autonomous agent tasks. Users should have prior experience with IoT environments.
aiSummary.gettingStarted: Refer to the repository documentation for building the macOS desktop application or CLI.
